frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/useOfflineSupport.ts:352-357 — processQueue() permanently DROPS a terminally-failed offline mutation from the sync queue with only a `console.error('Action failed after max retries:', action)`. An action is terminal when it is `permanent` (a 4xx, reasonable to drop) OR `action.retries >= 3` (transient 5xx/network — NOT safe to drop). At line ~400 the queue is rebuilt keeping only `!succeededIds.has(a.id) && !terminalFailureIds.has(a.id)`, so the failed action's PAYLOAD (e.g. an offline-created fault report from screens/faults/ReportFaultScreen.tsx, or a document action) is discarded with no dead-letter store and no per-item retry affordance.

Surfacing is aggregate-only: App.tsx:82 fires processQueue() fire-and-forget on reconnect; syncProgress.failed (App.tsx:334) feeds PendingSyncIndicator.tsx which renders a t('sync.failed') count. The user sees 'N failed' but cannot see WHICH items failed nor recover/re-submit them — after 3 transient-failure sync cycles genuine user work is silently lost even though the server may have only been temporarily unavailable.

Reachability traced: App.tsx onReconnect useEffect -> processQueue -> per-action executeQueuedAction catch -> retries++ -> retries>=3 terminal drop. Confidence medium (static; the 4xx branch is intentional and correct, the transient-exhaustion branch is the data-loss concern). Suggested fix: move retry-exhausted (non-permanent) actions to a persisted dead-letter list with an explicit user-visible 'retry / discard' surface rather than dropping them, and/or exempt idempotent CREATEs from the 3-cycle cap.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/compliance/pages/ContentModerationPage.tsx:128-146 — handleTakeAction() collects the moderation action via window.prompt('Enter action type (remove, restrict, warn, approve):') and passes the free-text result straight into the mutation as `action_type: actionType as 'remove' | 'restrict' | 'warn' | 'approve'`. frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/settings/pages/SessionsPage.tsx:84 — `const sessions = (sessionsQuery.data?.sessions ?? []) as unknown as SessionRow[];` force-casts the auth API sessions response to the local SessionRow[] via the double `as unknown as` escape hatch, bypassing all structural checking between the generated SDK type and SessionRow. Immediately after, code reads `s.isCurrent` (:85, and current-session highlighting / revoke UI downstream). If the SDK field is snake_case (is_current) or the shape drifts, `s.isCurrent` is silently undefined, so 'this device' detection and the revoke-all-other-sessions affordance can mis-identify the current session on a security-sensitive session-management screen. The cast hides exactly the kind of API-contract drift the generated client exists to catch.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/agencies.rs:373-401 — create_invitation (wired at line 38: POST /api/v1/agencies/{id}/invitations) performs NO membership/role check before calling the repo, unlike its siblings update_agency (line 268) and update_branding (line 322) which both call super::agency_imports::check_agency_membership. Verified in-file this run: create_invitation goes straight to reality_portal_repo.create_invitation(agency_id, principal.user_id, data). The repo method (backend/crates/db/src/repositories/reality_portal/agencies.rs:228-253) does an unconditional INSERT with no authorization, so the handler's 403 mapping for 'permission'/'unauthorized' (agencies.rs:390) is dead code.

Impact: any authenticated portal user (RequestPrincipal) can create an invitation for ANY agency id with an attacker-controlled email AND role (CreateAgencyInvitation.role: Option<String>, COALESCE default 'realtor' — so 'admin'/'owner' is accepted). Combined with accept_invitation (agencies.rs:421) the attacker invites their own email as 'owner', receives the token in the 201 response body, accepts it, and gains membership/control of an arbitrary agency — broken-access-control privilege escalation.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/agencies.rs:421-448 — accept_invitation adds the calling principal.user_id as an agency member based solely on a valid, unexpired token (repo accept_invitation at backend/crates/db/src/repositories/reality_portal/agencies.rs:256+ looks up the invitation by token then inserts the member) and never verifies that the authenticated user's email matches the invitation's target `email` column. Any authenticated user holding a token meant for someone else joins the agency with the invitation's role. Independently limited by token unguessability (UUIDv4), but directly compounds code-review-reality-server-invite-authz since the attacker mints and reads their own token.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/agencies.rs:345-358 — list_members (GET /api/v1/agencies/{id}/members) has NO principal extractor (verified: signature is only State + Path<Uuid>) and calls get_agency_members(id) for any agency id, yet its OpenAPI doc advertises a 401 response (agencies.rs:342) that can never occur. Unauthenticated callers enumerate an agency's full membership roster (RealityAgencyMember: user_id, role, is_active, joined_at) for any agency UUID. Lower severity than the invitation issues since the DTO carries no name/email PII, but it is an unintended unauthenticated read that contradicts the documented contract.
